mappings.mapping_description: MAESTRO directly addresses EO-01 through two of its three core research pillars and the cross-cutting tool orchestration layer. Pillar 1 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning) advances planning mechanisms by developing a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with verifiable intermediate states, integrates search-based algorithms (MCTS, hierarchical task networks) with LLM-driven heuristic evaluation, and supports self-correction through plan monitoring and replanning — directly improving agent autonomy and robustness. Pillar 2 (Adaptive Memory Architecture) advances memory management by unifying working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory into a persistent architecture with a memory controller that manages information flow across stores, enabling coherent long-term agent behaviour — directly improving reliability over extended interactions. The External Tool and API Orchestration Layer enhances reliability by grounding agent reasoning in verified external data and providing principled fallback/recovery mechanisms for tool failures. The concept corpus uses the exact vocabulary of EO-01: 'autonomy', 'robustness', 'reliability', 'planning mechanisms', 'memory management', and 'reasoning capabilities' all appear verbatim or as direct equivalents in concept_note.md and project_summary.json.

mappings.mapping_description: MAESTRO directly addresses EO-02 through Pillar 3 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination) and the multi-agent extensions of the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer. Pillar 3 develops multi-agent coordination protocols enabling heterogeneous agents to collaborate on shared objectives through: a formal task-delegation protocol with provable convergence guarantees; conflict resolution mechanisms for contested resources and inconsistent world models; and auditable multi-agent interaction traces. The External Tool and API Orchestration Layer extends multi-agent capability by governing shared tool access, delegated tool invocation, and conflict resolution when multiple agents require the same external resource. The concept corpus uses the exact vocabulary of EO-02: 'multi-agent frameworks', 'protocols', 'decentralised coordination', and 'collaboration' all appear verbatim in concept_note.md and strategic_positioning.md. The manufacturing demonstrator (multi-agent process optimisation) and logistics demonstrator (multi-actor supply chain coordination) provide concrete validation contexts demonstrating capabilities beyond individual agents.
